items.title: Tom Scott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2022 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: So there was this book the Carroll Knudson book.

ctx.x: That’s correct. It was, yeah, it was a whole separate science of how to make some hit, some chord or some thing in the music hit at exactly the right time where the gun is fired or the car takes off or there’s some bit of, you know, so there was a whole lot of

mathematics involved. Once you decide what the right tempo is, what feels right, you can then determine what that is in terms of a metronome beat, which of course you have to translate to frames per second, a 12-frame click — well film runs at 24 frames per second. So a 24-frame click meant it went one click every second. A 12-frame click, half of that, would be a click every half a second. And then everything in between. So there was this book the Carroll Knudson book. And this guy should have gotten an award…

Regarding themes for the subsequent shows you did after “Dan August,” music sometimes can convey emotions and sometimes music is just music. So was your task to read the description of what this show’s going to be about, maybe about the characters you know, it’s a cop but he’s got marital trouble, he’s got a young kid etcetera, and how much did the music you were trying to write reflect the story?
